findings.title: Switchyard base_name rename breaks compat
findings.problem: The switchyard base_name values for two Claude models were renamed from the long descriptive form (e.g. 'claude-sonnet-4-6-switchyard-claude-4-5-haiku-signal') to short opaque aliases (e.g. 'sy-signal-claude'), but tests/codemie/configs/test_llm_config.py's _DIAL_EXPECTED_ROUTER_NAMES frozenset still holds the old names, and test_dial_config_generates_expected_router_names is not skipped since the DIAL config file exists.
findings.impact: test_dial_config_generates_expected_router_names will fail on the next test run; this also contradicts the spec's explicit non-goal that the base_name scheme stay 1:1 so already-stored assistant.llm_model references keep resolving, risking broken resolution for any existing assistants configured against the old alias names.
findings.recommendation: Either revert to the original base_name values, or update _DIAL_EXPECTED_ROUTER_NAMES to the new aliases and confirm/migrate any persisted assistant.llm_model references before shipping the rename.

findings.title: Optional[X] mixed with X | None unions
findings.problem: This file mixes typing.Optional[float]/Optional[UUID]/Optional[LLMResult]/Optional[dict[str, Any]] (lines 72, 91, 150, 152, 168, 178, 324, 397, 406, 467) with modern 'X | None' unions used elsewhere in the same file.
findings.impact: Violates the documented code-quality.md Types And Imports standard (blocking per the standards audit); inconsistent typing style diverges from the modern-union convention the rest of this diff follows.
findings.recommendation: Replace the remaining Optional[X] annotations with X | None and drop the now-unused Optional import.

findings.title: No hard-fail when a router base_name reaches execution
findings.problem: get_llm_by_credentials() has no check rejecting a router base_name (Switchyard or LiteLLM-auto-router alias) that reaches it directly instead of a concrete deployment; the acceptance criterion requiring this hard-fail is unmet anywhere in the current codebase, not just in this diff.
findings.impact: If a router alias ever reaches this function (misconfiguration, a future caller bypassing build_chat_model_for/RouterProxySession), the failure mode is whatever get_model_details/get_litellm_chat_model does with an alias it wasn't built for, instead of a clear, intentional rejection.
findings.recommendation: Confirm with the ticket owner whether this guard belongs to this decoupling ticket or a separate one. Note: most of this acceptance run's other 'fail' criteria (to_llm_model removal, LlmRouterOption/get_allowed_router_options, the llm_config.py domain-model additions) are already satisfied by code this diff doesn't touch, suggesting the acceptance lens's spec document describes a broader/different-phase scope than this diff - worth confirming the correct spec artifact is attached to this ticket.

findings.title: counterfactual_model now always disclosed to clients
findings.problem: counterfactual_model was newly added to _ROUTING_HEADER_FIELDS (it was never in this header set before the move from enterprise/switchyard/proxy.py), and combined with LiteLLMRouter.routing_info() now setting requested_model/counterfactual_model unconditionally (see CR-007), every proxy response for a model declared as a LiteLLM auto-router now unconditionally carries x-codemie-requested-model and x-codemie-routing-counterfactual-model, even when no routing actually occurred for that call.
findings.impact: A new, always-on external disclosure of internal pricing-baseline/model-alias information to every API client for these models, where previously this only existed internally.
findings.recommendation: Only emit these two headers when real routing signal is present (e.g. gate on routed_model is not None), or confirm this disclosure is an intended, reviewed API surface change.

findings.title: Unparameterized dict annotation
findings.problem: event_data: dict = json.loads(...) uses a bare, unparameterized dict annotation.
findings.impact: Violates the documented code-quality.md Types And Imports standard (blocking per the standards audit), which prefers parameterized generics over bare dict/list.
findings.recommendation: Annotate as event_data: dict[str, object] = json.loads(...).

findings.title: Body-rewrite check compares against wrong baseline
findings.problem: decide_and_rewrite() compares chosen_model != requested_model, where requested_model = request_body.get('model'); the replaced apply_router_routing compared chosen_model != router_name, the resolved alias actually passed in, not the raw body field.
findings.impact: When a routable request body lacks a top-level 'model' key (_extract_model falls back to URL path params or the CLI header), requested_model is None, so the comparison is always true: decide_and_rewrite always takes the override branch, unconditionally injecting a 'model' field and logging a misleading '[ROUTING-PROXY] Override None -> X' even when the decision matched the originally resolved alias exactly. Reachability of this input shape on a live request path was not fully confirmed (v1/chat/completions and v1/messages normally carry 'model' in the body per the OpenAI/Anthropic contract).
findings.recommendation: Compare chosen_model against the originally resolved router_name (pass it into decide_and_rewrite or store it on the session) instead of request_body.get('model').

findings.title: LiteLLMRouter.routing_info() never reports empty
findings.problem: routing_info() now builds RoutingInfo(counterfactual_model=self.counterfactual_model, requested_model=self.router_name) unconditionally from router-owned state, instead of only from actual response headers as the previous extract() did (requested_model used to come from meta.router_model_name, an actual x-litellm-router-model-name response header). RoutingInfo.is_empty() checks 'all fields None', so it can now never be True for any LiteLLM-router-declared model.
findings.impact: Defeats two downstream guards that rely on is_empty() to detect 'no real routing signal': TokensCalculationCallback.on_llm_end's cache-hit skip (tokens_callback.py:361, 'if cache_hit and display_routing.is_empty(): return') no longer fires, so a cache hit with no real x-litellm-router-* headers now always records a near-empty llm_run.routing instead of being skipped; and proxy_router.py's _queue_routing_metric (line 1229, 'if proxy_routing.is_empty(): return') now always queues a routing analytics metric for every declared LiteLLM router alias even with zero real routing signal, polluting routing/cost analytics.
findings.recommendation: Only set requested_model/counterfactual_model when real routing headers are present, or change both downstream guards to check routed_model is None instead of is_empty().

Recorded decision by the ticket owner on 2026-09-22: accepted as-is. Per the ticket owner, LiteLLM's proxy contract guarantees x-litellm-router-routed-model on every response for a router-declared model, including cache hits (routing decision made before the cache lookup), so is_empty() correctly stays non-empty here rather than regressing — the routed_model-is-None alternative discussed would be equally always-false under this contract, so it was not adopted either. If that header were ever actually absent it would indicate an upstream LiteLLM/proxy failure worth investigating directly, not a case to silently skip. No code change requested.
